sources.citation: Baumann, Oscar. 1894. Durch Massailand zur Nilquelle. Reisen und Forschungen der Massai-Expedition des deutschen Antisklaverei-Komite in den Jahren 1891-1893. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. Anhang VII 'Sprachproben' (pp. 363ff.), 'Ndorobbo, Serengeti' on p. 366; ethnographic note pp. 167-168.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. p. 366 gives numerals 1-10, 15, 20, 30, two short texts with free German translation and 'kinavéta napó = ein Rind'. Many words carry an acute accent (eméta, emehoréta, imidátene, koraá, kavendá, totowó, tégenos, kópowa, ártam, napó, naudó) whose position varies (initial, antepenult, penult, final), but Baumann never says what the acute marks; his only orthographic remark (p. 363) is 'Als Orthographie wurde die Steer'sche Swahili-Schreibart angewandt.' This page is the entire attestation of the language.
